name: Sun City Girls
label: Drag City
lede: Two brothers from Michigan and a drummer they met at a Tempe pizza-parlor open mic, named for a retirement town, hated by punk crowds, and gone the day the drummer was.

eras.title: Named for a retirement town
eras.text: Alan and Richard Bishop, half-Lebanese brothers who had spent summers in Saginaw, Michigan, around their grandfather's all-night oud sessions, started a band in Phoenix and named it after Sun City, the retirees' town nearby. A drummer from California made it a trio, and a trip to Morocco pointed it at the rest of the world.

years.h: Alan and Richard Bishop start Sun City Girls in Phoenix
years.p: The brothers name the band after Sun City, Arizona, a planned community for retirees outside Phoenix.
years.xp: Richard Bishop grew up partly in Saginaw, Michigan, where their father ran a surplus store and their grandfather, a master oud player, hosted all-night jam sessions. Alan also played early on with Paris 1942, a group featuring [[Moe Tucker|66742cdb-d1c2-4546-8204-3ff36db12da9]] of [[The Velvet Underground|94b0fb9d-a066-4823-b2ec-af1d324bcfcf]], and briefly with [[JFA|ed1cc87f-1e93-48aa-ad09-e67ccb77be37]].

q: He was the first serious, true jazz musician that I spent any time with.
years.h: Charles Gocher walks into a Tempe pizza-joint open mic
years.p: [[Charles Gocher|a95e9a40-0be4-4741-b84b-200c3dc67a48]], a Californian who had played guitar in a Prescott acid-rock band called Cha Cha Billy, turns up at an open mic Alan Bishop hosts. He's recruited on the spot as drummer.
years.xp:
Gocher had been in Arizona since 1971 and later worked at Zia Records in Tempe. He said it took ten years, but he knew he'd meet people he'd feel empathy with.

Alan Bishop remembered him as the first serious jazz musician he'd spent time with. The lineup never changed again.

years.h: Sun City Girls land on Placebo's Amuck compilation
years.p: Phoenix label Placebo Records puts Sun City Girls on Amuck. They end up the only band besides [[JFA|ed1cc87f-1e93-48aa-ad09-e67ccb77be37]] on all three Placebo compilations.

years.h: The Bishop brothers go to Morocco and tape the radio
years.p: Richard Bishop stays three weeks, Alan two months, recording shortwave broadcasts and jamming with local players. Twenty years later the tapes become Sublime Frequencies' Radio Morocco.

eras.title: Sandwiches from the floor
eras.text: Sun City Girls were booked into punk shows and gave punk crowds surreal theater, improv comedy and noise instead. Placebo Records put out their first LPs, and they toured the country with JFA, an odd pairing that confused both audiences.

years.src: Perfect Sound Forever · Phoenix New Times
years.h: Sun City Girls, the debut LP on Placebo
years.p: Placebo owner Tony Victor pays for the band's first album.

years.h: Sun City Girls tour the country with JFA
years.p: The skate punks of [[JFA|ed1cc87f-1e93-48aa-ad09-e67ccb77be37]] and the Sun City Girls hit the road together, a mismatch Phoenix New Times' oral history calls an odd pairing.

years.h: Opening for Black Flag, Richard Bishop eats the sandwiches thrown at him
years.p: A [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]] crowd hates Sun City Girls and pelts them. Richard Bishop eats the sandwiches off the floor, and by the end skinheads are on stage blowing horns with the band.
years.xp: Richard Bishop told Perfect Sound Forever the audience absolutely hated them and started throwing things. The band didn't stop, and the crowd ended up in the act.

years.h: Grotto of Miracles, the second Placebo LP
years.p: Sun City Girls' second album, again on Placebo. Alan Bishop was working in Placebo's office and warehouse by then.

years.h: Horse Cock Phepner takes aim at Arizona's governor
years.p: Perfect Sound Forever called it a filthy look into the Evan Mecham and Ronald Reagan era. Gocher's clear-hair concept first shows up here.

years.cap: Mill Avenue, Tempe, across from Grady Gammage
years.h: Torch of the Mystics is taped in a Tempe front room
years.p: On a borrowed 8-track in a friend's house on Mill Avenue, across from ASU's Grady Gammage Auditorium. Weeks after the sessions, a car crashes through the front window. No one is hurt.
years.xp: Some of the ambient and spoken-word pieces were recorded in the front yard. Richard Bishop played a 1940s Oahu lap steel, and the line hiss had to be cleaned up in the mix.

eras.title: Seattle, and a flood of tapes
eras.text: The band moved to Seattle around 1991 and put out records at a rate few could follow: LPs on Nick Schultz's Majora label, then their own Abduction imprint, double and triple CDs, and shows where a mop became a horse.

years.h: Torch of the Mystics comes out
years.p: The Tempe front-room sessions become the Sun City Girls album fans hunt for most. Richard Bishop said they knew it was a powerful release.

years.h: Sun City Girls move to Seattle
years.p: The band relocates from Arizona to Seattle and later sets up a shared compound in the Ballard neighborhood.

years.h: Dawn of the Devi on Majora
years.p: The first of several records for Nick Schultz's Seattle label Majora, followed by Bright Surroundings Dark Beginnings in 1993.

years.h: Engineer Scott Colburn sees 35 Sun City Girls shows in a row
years.p: Scott Colburn starts recording the band at his Gravelvoice Studios. The Stranger says he watched 35 straight shows and came away a believer in improvisation.

years.h: A globe on a pogo stick, a mop for a horse
years.p: Sun City Girls shows now mean props: bedsheets, a fake campfire, a mop ridden as a horse. Charles Gocher's drums fly apart as he plays.
years.xp: Gocher told Seattle Weekly he played drums like Harry Houdini escaping. He called the whole thing an escapist reality.

years.h: 330,003 Crossdressers from Beyond the Rig Veda
years.p: One of two Sun City Girls double CDs in the same year, alongside Dante's Disneyland Inferno.

years.h: Box of Chameleons, a triple CD
years.p: Three discs of Sun City Girls, the same year Charles Gocher releases his solo album Pint-Sized Spartacus.

eras.title: Radio from everywhere
eras.text: The Bishops' travels turned into a second project: Sublime Frequencies, a label for radio broadcasts and field recordings from Africa, Asia and the Middle East. Richard started playing solo, and the trio cut what would be its last album.

years.h: The Bishops co-found Sublime Frequencies
years.p: Alan and Richard Bishop start the Seattle label with Hisham Mayet, releasing shortwave radio collages and field recordings. Radio Morocco draws on the 1983 trip.

years.h: Richard Bishop goes solo as Sir Richard Bishop
years.p: [[Sir Richard Bishop|a444f8ff-2f8b-438b-a680-32c1f393244b]] begins touring Europe, Australia and the U.S. alone with an acoustic guitar. Drag City signs him in 2007.

years.h: The trio records Funeral Mariachi in Seattle
years.p: Sun City Girls' last sessions with Charles Gocher. Gocher has been fighting cancer for two years and has told almost no one.

eras.title: No Sun City Girls without Charlie
eras.text: Gocher's death ended the band. The Bishops kept the name off any new work, toured his films instead, and spent the next years putting out the last album and reissuing the old ones on Abduction.

years.h: Charles Gocher dies of cancer in Seattle at 54
years.p: [[Charles Gocher|a95e9a40-0be4-4741-b84b-200c3dc67a48]] dies after a three-year fight with cancer he kept private. Alan and Richard Bishop say they won't perform or record as Sun City Girls again.
years.xp:
A private memorial was held at the band's Ballard compound.

Alan Bishop told Seattle Weekly they simply weren't using the name any more, because it couldn't be.

years.h: The Brothers Unconnected tour plays Gocher's films
years.p: The Bishops tour the U.S. and Canada as The Brothers Unconnected, screening Gocher's videos and playing Sun City Girls songs acoustic, including some he wrote.

years.h: Mister Lonely soundtrack on Drag City
years.p: Sun City Girls and [[J. Spaceman|e7183895-fe12-4bce-8cdb-bdd8eaa31986]] of [[Spiritualized|65041e06-83d2-4987-ae52-c17a915fc82a]] score Harmony Korine's film. Drag City issues it as DC360.

years.h: Funeral Mariachi, the final Sun City Girls album
years.p: The 2006 sessions come out on Abduction, with [[Eyvind Kang|a4772e12-bda2-4df0-9c3c-8733933865d8]] and Jessika Kenney guesting and a cover of [[Ennio Morricone|a16e47f5-aa54-47fe-87e4-bb8af91a9fdd]]'s Come Maddalena. Pitchfork gives it 7.4.

years.h: Abduction reissues Torch of the Mystics
years.p: Alan Bishop's Abduction label puts the long-sought 1990 album back out, remastered by Mark Gergis.
